injuries.longComment: Nye will miss a fourth consecutive game Wednesday because of a knee injury, with her next opportunity to return coming on Friday for the rematch. With that in mind, Nye hasn't logged more than five minutes in a game this season, so her absence won't significantly impact the rotation.
injuries.shortComment: Nye (Knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Golden State.

injuries.longComment: Jones, who hasn't yet been cleared for 5-on-5 drills, continues to make significant progress in her rehab from right knee surgery. The star center still doesn't carry a firm timetable for a return, but it sounds like she'll have a chance to return at some point in early July. Until Jones is ready to return, Naz Hillmon should continue to play a big role in the frontcourt alongside Angel Reese.
injuries.shortComment: The Dream expect Jones (knee) to resume team activities in the coming weeks, per Myles Ehrlich of Winsidr.com.

injuries.longComment: Cloud was a late addition to Chicago's injury report. If the veteran guard is unable to play, the team is likely to rely more on Sydney Taylor.
injuries.shortComment: Cloud (illness) is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Fire.

injuries.longComment: Vandersloot is still recovering from the right knee surgery she underwent last June to repair a torn ACL, and there's been no indication that she's close to a return.
injuries.shortComment: Vandersloot (knee) does not have a timetable to return to the court.

injuries.longComment: Carrington underwent left foot surgery in April and there's been no indication that she's close to making her season debut.
injuries.shortComment: Carrington (foot) remains without a timetable to return.

injuries.longComment: The season-ending knee injury is a devastating development for Jackson and the Sky, as the 25-year-old forward was well on her way to a career-best campaign. Through Chicago's first four games, Jackson averaged 18.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 29.5 minutes per contest. After Jackson's early exit in Sunday's contest, Aicha Coulibaly opened the second half with the starters and looks to be the most likely candidate to move into the top unit for the Sky's next game Wednesday versus the Wings.
injuries.shortComment: The Sky announced Tuesday that Jackson will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL in her left knee during Sunday's 86-79 win over the Lynx.

injuries.longComment: After starting the last nine games, Rivers reverted to a bench role Monday and sprained her ankle. Her next chance to play will come Friday against the Mystics. If Rivers is forced to miss time, Charlisse Leger-Walker and Gianna Kneepkens would be candidates for increased playing time.
injuries.shortComment: Rivers won't return to Monday's game against the Sky due to a left ankle sprain, and she'll finish with four points (0-2 FG, 4-4 FT), three rebounds and one block in 13 minutes.

injuries.longComment: Jackson is signed to a developmental contract and limited to 12 regular-season appearances. She won't suit up in order to preserve her eligibility moving ahead.
injuries.shortComment: Jackson (coach's decision) won't play in Monday's game against Chicago.

injuries.longComment: This will mark Van Lith's fifth consecutive game on the inactive list. Her next chance to play will come Friday versus the Mystics.
injuries.shortComment: Van Lith (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's matchup with the Sky.

injuries.longComment: Sims hasn't played since the 104-96 loss to the Sparks on June 5. While Sims remains sidelined, Aziaha James should continue to see more minutes.
injuries.shortComment: Sims (ankle) is listed as out for Monday's game against the Storm.

injuries.longComment: Rupert signed a multi-year contract with Golden State during the offseason and missed the start of training camp due to an overseas commitment. Her status for the 2026 regular season now appears to be in jeopardy due to her pregnancy. The 24-year-old made 21 regular-season appearances (11 starts) for the Valkyries last year and averaged 9.3 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 23.1 minutes per game. If Rupert is sidelined in 2026, Janelle Salaun, Kiah Stokes and Laeticia Amihere are candidates to see increased work.
injuries.shortComment: Rupert is pregnant, and the Valkyries have filed for a replacement contract ahead of the 2026 season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports Thursday.

injuries.longComment: It's unknown when Barker will be cleared to suit up after missing the last three games due to a leg injury. However, even when the rookie is healthy enough to return, that doesn't mean she will see action, considering she has yet to make her WNBA debut.
injuries.shortComment: Barker (leg) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against the Liberty.

injuries.longComment: Carter will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to an illness, and her next chance to suit up will come Thursday against Dallas. In the meantime, Kierstan Bell and Brianna Turner could see increased playing time off the bench.
injuries.shortComment: Carter (illness) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Liberty.

injuries.longComment: Evans remains without a clear timetable for a return and has yet to make her season debut due to a left leg injury. She can be considered week-to-week until the Aces offer an update on her progress.
injuries.shortComment: Evans (leg) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Lynx.

injuries.longComment: Brink will miss a third consecutive contest due to a left ankle sprain. Head coach Lynne Roberts said last Wednesday that the 24-year-old is expected to remain on the inactive list for more than just a short-term stint, so she can be considered week-to-week until the Sparks offer an update on her progress. While Brink is sidelined, Jihyun Park, Emma Cannon and Laura Ziegler are candidates for increased playing time.
injuries.shortComment: Brink (ankle) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Tempo.

injuries.longComment: This is a brutal blow for Plum and the Sparks. Based on this initial timetable, the earliest possible return would be July 28 against the Liberty. Through 12 appearances, she has posted averages of 23.9 points and 6.4 assists on 52.7 percent shooting from the field. In her absence, the Sparks will need to lean more on Ariel Atkins and Erica Wheeler.
injuries.shortComment: Plum has suffered a lower left leg injury and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Mitchell Hansen of CanisHoopus.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Head coach Cheryl Reeve said Wednesday that Collier is "doing basketball things" but isn't yet cleared for team-related activities. The superstar forward underwent surgery on her left ankle March 24 and was expected to return to on-court activities in early June, but she remains without a concrete timeline for her season debut.
injuries.shortComment: Collier (ankle) has yet to resume full on-court activities, per Andrew Dukowitz of ZoneCoverage.com.

injuries.longComment: Juhasz is dealing with a right mid-foot sprain, per Borzi, and will miss at least the next five games, including Thursday's clash against Toronto. A more exact timeline for her return should come into focus as she begins to clear hurdles in her rehab.
injuries.shortComment: Juhasz (foot) is expected to remain out for another 2-to-3 weeks, Pat Borzi of MinnPost reports.

injuries.longComment: Cechova suffered a non-contact injury during Thursday's 90-86 win over Dallas and required assistance off the floor. After undergoing an MRI, she was diagnosed with a torn ACL, ending her season. The 21-year-old rookie appeared in three games, and she will finish the 2026 campaign by averaging 8.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 0.3 steals and 0.7 blocks across 17.3 minutes. With Cechova sidelined, Anastasiia Kosu could be first in line to see more action.
injuries.shortComment: Cechova (knee) was diagnosed with a torn ACL in her right knee and will undergo surgery, Meghan L. Hall of USA Today reports. She will miss the remainder of the season.

injuries.shortComment: day-to-day

injuries.longComment: Maley will be inactive in order to preserve her eligibility on a developmental contract. Her next chance to suit up will come Thursday against the Storm.
injuries.shortComment: Maley (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Aces.

injuries.longComment: Fauthoux will sit out Tuesday's contest in an effort to preserve her eligibility under a developmental contract. Her next chance to play will come Thursday in Seattle.
injuries.shortComment: Fauthoux (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Aces.

injuries.longComment: Mack was unable to shake her questionable tag for this contest and will sit out for the first time this season. With this news, the Mercury could lean more on Valeriane Ayayi.
injuries.shortComment: Mack (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against the Fever.

injuries.longComment: Akoa Makani will miss a third straight game due to a left hamstring injury, and her next chance to play will come Saturday in Toronto. Alexa Held will likely remain in the starting five in Akoa Makani's stead.
injuries.shortComment: Akoa Makani (hamstring) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game in Indiana.

injuries.longComment: According to Hayden Cilley of ClutchPoints.com, head coach Nate Tibbetts said pregame that Nogic is not with the team for personal reasons. She can be considered out indefinitely until the Mercury offer another update. With Nogic unavailable, Alexa Held is likely to see increased playing time moving forward.
injuries.shortComment: The Mercury temporarily suspended Nogic's (not with team) contract Saturday.

injuries.longComment: This is a tough blow for Whitcomb and the Mercury as she will now miss the first month or so of the WNBA season. Whitcomb served as a part-time starter during her first season in Phoenix last year, averaging 9.1 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.5 assists in 23.9 minutes per game across 43 regular-season appearances (20 starts). Kiana Williams could see an uptick in minutes with this news.
injuries.shortComment: Whitcomb will undergo an arthroscopy on Thursday to remove a loose body in her left knee. She will be re-evaluated in four to six weeks, Shane Young of the Mercury's official site reports.

injuries.longComment: Samuelson is dealing with left foot inflammation, and the Fire should have a better idea about her status closer to Wednesday's tipoff. Nyadiew Puoch stands out as the most likely candidate for a large role if Samuelson ends up sitting out.
injuries.shortComment: Samuelson (foot) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Sky.

injuries.longComment: The right ankle sprain is a new concern for Leite, who is in danger of missing her first game since May 18. The 22-year-old guard has scored in double figures in five consecutive contests, averaging 13.6 points, 6.6 assists and 3.6 rebounds in 25.6 minutes per game during that span. If she's unable to play Wednesday, Sarah Ashlee Barker, Teja Oblak and Holly Winterburn would be candidates for increased burn, especially if Karlie Samuelson (foot) is downgraded from questionable to out as well.
injuries.shortComment: Leite (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Sky.

injuries.longComment: day-to-day
injuries.shortComment: day-to-day

injuries.longComment: Magbegor was given a 6-to-8-week timetable in April due to a right foot injury, and she's progressing toward a return to game action. However, there's still no clear timetable for her return, so the 26-year-old can be considered week-to-week until the Storm offer another update on her progress.
injuries.shortComment: Head coach Sonia Raman said Monday that Magbegor (foot) is progressing well and has advanced to 5-on-5 work, Roberta Rodrigues of Beta Basket reports.

injuries.longComment: Horston will miss her third consecutive game Monday, and for now, she should be considered questionable for Thursday's matchup with the Liberty. Jade Melbourne (foot), who had been starting in Horston's absence, is questionable for Monday's game, and if she can't give it a go, Katie Lou Samuelson would have an opportunity to start.
injuries.shortComment: Horston (foot) is out for Monday's meeting with the Wings.

injuries.longComment: Sykes is dealing with a plantar fascia injury and will remain sidelined for the Tempo. In the meantime, Toronto will likely lean more on Julie Allemand and Kia Nurse.
injuries.shortComment: Sykes (foot) will be re-evaluated in the coming weeks, according to WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland.

injuries.longComment: The injury was previously considered a Grade 2 sprain, so Rice is trending in the right direction. According to Copeland, Rice will be re-evaluated in the coming weeks. Julie Allemand will likely see an uptick in minutes in the meantime.
injuries.shortComment: Rice (ankle) remains sidelined by a Grade 3 left ankle sprain, according to WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland.
